sentences.text: This final lesson pulls together the differences between Inland and International rules, because they produce a large share of exam questions.
International maneuvering signals announce action being taken whenever a power-driven vessel maneuvers in sight of another.
Inland signals propose an intention and need agreement between power-driven vessels meeting or crossing within half a mile.
International overtaking signals are used in narrow channels and start with two prolonged blasts.
Inland overtaking signals are one or two short blasts, in any waters.
Inland, a radio agreement replaces the whistle signals, and a vessel leaving a berth sounds one prolonged blast.
Inland maneuvering lights may be white or yellow.
